subject: general
question: The planning in the real sense began with __________five year plan in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** of India marked the beginning of real planning in the sense of establishing a structured framework for economic development. 
 
• The plan was introduced in the year **1956** and was primarily focused on **industrialization and the development of heavy industries**.
 
• The Second Plan was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, created by Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**, which emphasized the importance of capital goods in economic growth. 
 
• This plan aimed to achieve a **self-reliant economy** by reducing dependence on imports and promoting domestic production. 
 
• The focus shifted from agriculture to industries, which was a significant step in India's economic trajectory. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• India adopted the **planning model** from the Soviet Union, with the **First Five-Year Plan** (1951-1956) focusing on agriculture and irrigation.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956-1961) emphasized industrialization and aimed at laying the foundation for a modern economy.
 
• Subsequent plans focused on diverse sectors such as poverty alleviation, energy generation, education, and rural development.
 
 
 
• **Mahalanobis Model:**
 
 
• The model developed by **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis** focused on the importance of **heavy industries** for long-term growth.
 
• It advocated allocating resources to industries that produce capital goods, which are essential for sustained economic development.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan Outcomes:**
 
 
• Increased focus on **steel production**, with the establishment of plants like **Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur**.
 
• Expansion of public sector enterprises and promotion of self-reliance in industrial production.
 
• Significant growth in infrastructure and development of transport systems.
 
 
 
• **Shift from Agriculture to Industry:**
 
 
• The Second Plan marked a shift from agricultural development to industrialization as the primary driver of economic growth.
 
• While agriculture remained important, the focus was on creating a balanced economy with strong industrial and agricultural bases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• The **Planning Commission of India** was established in **1950** under the leadership of **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru** to formulate and monitor Five-Year Plans.
 
• It aimed to assess resources, identify key sectors for development, and ensure balanced growth across the country.
 
 
 
• **Key Industries Developed:**
 
 
• Heavy industries such as steel, cement, and machine tools were prioritized during the Second Plan.
 
• These industries were considered crucial for laying the foundation of a **self-reliant economy**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Philosophy:**
 
 
• The Second Plan reflected the vision of **Nehruvian socialism**, which emphasized public sector growth and equal distribution of wealth.
 
• It was believed that state intervention in key industries would help reduce inequalities and promote inclusive growth.
